_limits_comment: Every measurement below declares limits (issue #154). Without them a
`klt pex` delta[] row's `status: pass` means only that both legs produced
a number -- not that the extracted value is anywhere near the schematic
one; `klt pex` grades a row against the *extracted*-side value's own
declared limits (see klayout-tools' pex.py `_row_status`).
Every bound below is derived from two things this file or the ratified
spec already states, never invented here:
vout_*_v            -- the ratified `Output` row of spec/target-spec.md,
verbatim.
vin_minus_vout_*_v  -- NOT the ratified `Dropout @ 50 mA` row. Reading
that row onto this measurement is a category
error: `Iload` is swept at a FIXED `vvin`, so
V(VIN)-V(VOUT) here is the supply-to-output
HEADROOM at that corner's supply, not the dropout
voltage (dropout is VIN swept down until VOUT
leaves regulation -- that is sim/dropout-vs-load's
testbench, not this one). With VIN held at one of
this request's own `corners.supply_v.vvin` values
and VOUT bounded by the ratified `Output` row, the
headroom of an in-spec part is bounded exactly by
those two declarations:
min = min(vvin) - max(Output) = 2.97 - 1.836
max = max(vvin) - min(Output) = 3.63 - 1.764
So this row adds a physicality check (a negative
or collapsed headroom fails) without asserting a
spec line this testbench cannot measure.
Consequence, stated plainly: the vout_* bounds are *spec* bounds, and
measurements/characterization.md already records the schematic-side
implementation as FAIL against the Output row at some PVT corners. A
failing row here is therefore not automatically an extraction artifact --
read it against the same corner's schematic_value in delta[] before
attributing it to the layout.
